title: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands in the UK in time for Christmas shopping
excerpt: Meta has launched Muse, its personal AI agent, in the UK with Sainsbury's, Argos, M&S, Currys, and easyJet plugged in, on the day the FCA set out its agentic AI rules.
content_html:
Meta’s personal AI agent Muse arrived in the UK today, pitched squarely at the festive to-do list. Unlike Meta AI, which chats and answers questions, Muse connects to other apps and acts. It can build a grocery basket, book a flight, chase a refund, or buy the presents.

Several of Britain’s biggest retailers are plugged in from day one. Sainsbury’s lets the agent plan meals and fill grocery orders, while Argos has connected more than 150,000 products, with M&S, Currys, Debenhams, and easyJet on board too. Muse runs as a standalone app, on the web, and inside WhatsApp.

Muse is for “doing the Christmas shopping and searching for a cheaper energy deal”, among other chores, Meta said in a statement.

Purchases go through Link, a wallet for AI agents built by Stripe that holds payment credentials, and buying anything requires the user’s approval. The shop still processes the transaction; the agent does the preparation.

The agent launched in the US in September and has been a hit there, ranking first and second on Google’s and Apple’s free app charts, the Guardian reported.

British regulators were waiting at the door when Muse arrived. It landed the same day the Financial Conduct Authority set out its expectations for agentic AI, rules that name social media platforms directly.

Earlier this month, the UK’s four digital regulators warned ministers that personal AI agents were about to launch in the country. The competition watchdog has secured changes to Meta’s terms, and the data regulator is monitoring the rollout, according to reports of the launch.

The timing gives retailers a live test of AI-led shopping through Black Friday and the Christmas trading period, with real customers and real money.
